title: A parallel page counter
description:
Count the words on several "pages" at once with a thread pool.

```
page-1: 40 words (0.10s)
page-2: 80 words (0.20s)
page-3: 120 words (0.30s)
Total: 240 words in 0.30s
```

starter.main.py:
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

pages = {"page-1": 0.1, "page-2": 0.2, "page-3": 0.3}


def fetch(name, delay):
    time.sleep(delay)
    words = int(delay * 400)
    return "word " * words


start = time.perf_counter()

hints: `futures = {pool.submit(fetch, name, delay): name for name, delay in pages.items()}` remembers which future belongs to which page.
`for future in as_completed(futures):` gives futures in the order they finish; `future.result()` is the text.
requirements: `fetch(name, delay)` pretends to download a page: it sleeps for `delay` seconds and returns some text.
Run all fetches with `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` and handle each result as it finishes (`as_completed`).
Print the total time: it should be close to the slowest page, not the sum of all of them.
stretch: Make one page raise an error and print `page-x failed: <error>` without stopping the others.
